newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish woman among four dead in Macedonia crash.
newsitem.headline: Finnish woman among four dead in Macedonia crash.

text.p: Three Finnish United Nations peacekeepers, one of them a woman, and their Canadian civilian pilot were killed in a helicopter crash in Macedonia on Saturday, the STT news agency said.

All three passengers -- a major, a captain and the battalion's female dentist -- as well as the pilot were killed when their helicopter plunged into a lake in Mavrovo, a national park south of the capital, Skopje. Two bodies were recovered.
The Finns were among 360 engaged in a U.N. operation with the pan-Nordic battalion.
The Finnish defence ministry later named the dead as major Risto Vuori, captain Tapani Kulmala and dentist Kaisa Arvola, STT said.
Volunteer women have been accepted for Finnish military service since 1995, and U.N. peacekeeping duty is voluntary.

The cause of the crash was unclear, STT said. But it quoted the defence ministry as saying it was clearly an aviation accident rather than the result of military action, possibly caused by a collision with an overhead power line.
